claim: The least squares method for calculating the best-fitting line through a two-dimensional scatter plot typically requires the user to assume that one of the variables depends on the other.
source_text: The use of the least squares method to calculate the best-fitting line through a two-dimensional scatter plot typically requires the user to assume that one of the variables depends on the other.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established understanding of the standard application of the least squares method in statistical analysis.

claim: In many cases the relationship between two variables is more complex, and it is not valid to say that one variable is independent and the other is dependent.
source_text: However, in many cases the relationship between the two variables is more complex, and it is not valid to say that one variable is independent and the other is dependent.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on general understanding of biological systems and logical inference about the complexity of variable relationships.

claim: The method of least squares was introduced by Legendre and Gauss more than two hundred years ago.
source_text: The straight line that constitutes the best fit to a set of data points in the x-y plane is typically calculated by minimizing the sum of the squares of the distances from the points to the line—a method that was introduced by Legendre and Gauss more than two hundred years ago.
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical fact about the origin of the least squares method, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: When one variable depends on another, the best-fitting line represents the expected value of the dependent variable (y) as a function of the independent variable (x), known as the regression of y on x.
source_text: If one variable, conventionally represented by the y-axis, is known to depend on the other variable, conventionally represented by the x-axis, then one generally calculates a best-fitting line that represents the expected value of the dependent variable (y) as a function of the independent variable (x): this is known as the regression of y on x.
evidence_reasoning: This describes standard statistical methodology for regression analysis.

claim: Except when all data points lie precisely on a straight line, the regression of y on x and the regression of x on y will not coincide.
source_text: Except in the limiting case in which all of the data points lie precisely on a straight line, these two best-fitting regression lines will not coincide.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mathematical property of regression lines that follows from the principles of least squares fitting.

claim: The Deming regression method is symmetric with respect to the two variables and makes no assumptions regarding dependence and independence.
source_text: The Deming regression method is symmetric with respect to the two variables and therefore makes no assumptions regarding dependence and independence
evidence_reasoning: This statement describes a property of Deming regression and is supported by citations to Cornbleet and Gochman, 1979; Linnet, 1993, 1998; Glaister, 2001.

claim: W. Edward Deming described the orthogonal regression method in the 1940s.
source_text: The latter name refers to the statistician W Edward Deming who described the method in the 1940s (Deming, 1943).
evidence_reasoning: This historical claim is supported by a citation to Deming, 1943.

claim: For a scatter plot where data points do not fall on a straight line, the best-fitting line calculated with vertical residuals will have a relatively shallow slope.
source_text: For a scatter plot in which the data points do not fall on a straight line, the best-fitting line calculated with vertical residuals will have a relatively shallow slope (Figure 1A)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1A and reflects mathematical properties of regression.

claim: The best-fitting line calculated with horizontal residuals will have a steeper slope than the line calculated with vertical residuals.
source_text: whereas the best-fitting line calculated with horizontal residuals will have a steeper slope (Figure 1B).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1B and reflects mathematical properties of regression.

claim: The best-fitting line calculated with perpendicular residuals will have an intermediate slope between the lines calculated with vertical and horizontal residuals.
source_text: The best-fitting line calculated with perpendicular residuals will have an intermediate slope (Figure 1C).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1C and reflects mathematical properties of orthogonal regression.

claim: The square of the correlation coefficient (R²) is equal to the slope of the regression line for y on x divided by the slope of the regression line for x on y.
source_text: It is conventional to calculate the square of the correlation coefficient (R2), which is equal to the slope of the regression line for y on x (that is, calculated using vertical residuals) divided by the slope of the regression line for x on y (horizontal residuals).
evidence_reasoning: This describes a mathematical relationship between correlation coefficient and regression slopes, representing established statistical knowledge.

claim: If data points fall on a straight line (R² = 1), the slopes of the two best-fitting lines (y on x and x on y) will be equal.
source_text: Thus, if the data points fall on a straight line (R2 = 1), the slopes of these two best-fitting lines will be equal.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mathematical consequence of perfect correlation, representing established statistical knowledge.

claim: With increasing scatter in the data (R² < 1), the slopes of the two best-fitting lines will diverge.
source_text: With increasing scatter in the data (R2 < 1), the slopes of the two best-fitting lines will diverge.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a mathematical property of regression lines as correlation decreases.

claim: If data points are completely uncorrelated (R² = 0), the best-fitting lines calculated with vertical and horizontal residuals will have slopes of 0 and infinity, respectively.
source_text: If the data points are completely uncorrelated (R2 = 0), then the best-fitting lines calculated with vertical and horizontal residuals will have slopes of 0 and infinity, respectively.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the mathematical behavior of regression lines in the case of zero correlation.

claim: The agreement between the three regression lines in the Ressler et al. data is relatively poor, as expected from the low values of R².
source_text: The agreement between the three lines is relatively poor, as expected from the low values of R2, where R is the correlation coefficient.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on visual inspection of Figure 2 and the mathematical relationship between R² and regression line divergence.

claim: PACAP secretion may alter the severity of PTSD symptoms.
source_text: For example, while it is possible that PACAP secretion may alter the severity of PTSD symptoms
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a possible causal relationship, indicated by the phrase 'it is possible that'.

claim: Stress associated with PTSD may alter PACAP secretion.
source_text: it is also possible that stress associated with PTSD may alter PACAP secretion.
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a possible causal relationship, indicated by the phrase 'it is also possible that'.

claim: PTSD symptoms and PACAP secretion may have no direct cause-and-effect relationship, with changes in neural circuitry altering both by distinct mechanisms.
source_text: Furthermore, it is possible that these two variables may have no direct cause-and-effect relationship, and that changes in neural circuitry alter stress level and PACAP secretion by distinct mechanisms.
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a possible alternative explanation, indicated by the phrase 'it is possible that'.

claim: The individual regression lines for y on x or x on y do not fully capture the trend in the data points within the scatter plots from Ressler et al.
source_text: Visual inspection of Figure 2 shows that the individual regression lines for y on x (green) or x on y (blue) do not fully capture the trend in the data points within any of the scatter plots.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on visual inspection of the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Plotting both regression lines (y on x and x on y) gives a fuller picture of the data.
source_text: Plotting both regression lines gives a fuller picture of the data
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the analysis of the data presentation in Figure 2.

claim: Comparing the slopes of the two regression lines provides a simple graphical assessment of the correlation coefficient.
source_text: comparing their slopes provides a simple graphical assessment of the correlation coefficient.
evidence_reasoning: This follows from the mathematical relationship between regression slopes and R² described earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The orthogonal regression line appears to more accurately describe the trend in the data compared to either of the ordinary least squares regression lines.
source_text: Plotting the orthogonal regression line (red) provides additional information because it makes no assumptions about the dependence or independence of the variables; as such, it appears to more accurately describe the trend in the data compared to either of the ordinary least squares regression lines.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on visual inspection and analysis of the data in Figure 2.

claim: The ordinary least squares method is well suited to the analysis of data sets in which one variable influences or predicts the value of a second variable.
source_text: The ordinary least squares method is well suited to the analysis of data sets in which one variable influences or predicts the value of a second variable.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established understanding of the appropriate application of ordinary least squares regression.

claim: In biological systems, causal relationships between variables are often complex.
source_text: In biological systems, where causal relationships between variables are often complex
evidence_reasoning: This reflects general scientific understanding of biological systems.

claim: Deciding that one variable depends on another may be somewhat arbitrary in biological systems.
source_text: In biological systems, where causal relationships between variables are often complex, deciding that one variable depends on the other may be somewhat arbitrary.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the complexity of biological systems and the difficulty of establishing clear causal relationships.

claim: Feedback regulation at the molecular, cellular or organ system level can undermine simple models of dependence and independence.
source_text: Moreover, even when a causal chain appears to be well established mechanistically, feedback regulation at the molecular, cellular or organ system level can undermine simple models of dependence and independence.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established understanding of feedback mechanisms in biological systems.

claim: Unless data analysis calls exclusively for a regression of y on x (or x on y), scatter plots should be presented with three best-fitting lines calculated with horizontal, vertical and perpendicular residuals.
source_text: Therefore, we would like to suggest that unless the data analysis calls exclusively for a regression of y on x (or x on y), scatter plots should be presented with three best-fitting lines–calculated with horizontal, vertical and perpendicular residuals–to facilitate a more balanced assessment of trends in the data.
evidence_reasoning: This is a recommendation based on the authors' analysis and reasoning presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The ordinary least squares method is ubiquitous in the analysis of two-dimensional scatter plots.
source_text: Given the ubiquity of the ordinary least squares method in the analysis of two-dimensional scatter plots
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the widespread use of ordinary least squares in scientific practice.

claim: Presenting three best-fitting lines should prove useful across the full range of biomedical sciences.
source_text: this small change in the standard approach to data presentation should prove useful across the full range of biomedical sciences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction about the utility of the proposed approach, based on the authors' reasoning but not yet empirically tested.

claim: The orthogonal or Deming regression is not available in Microsoft Excel.
source_text: The orthogonal or Deming regression shown by the red lines is not available in Microsoft Excel
evidence_reasoning: This is a factual statement about the capabilities of Microsoft Excel software.

claim: Deming regression can be calculated with Excel add-in freeware provided by Jon Peltier, with the 'r' statistics package, and with various commercial software packages including Analyse-it and MedCalc.
source_text: but it can be calculated with Excel add-in freeware provided by Jon Peltier (peltiertech.com/WordPress/deming-regression-utility), with the 'r' statistics package (www.r-project.org), and with various commercial software packages including Analyse-it (analyse-it.com) and MedCalc (www.medcalc.org/).
evidence_reasoning: This provides factual information about software tools that can perform Deming regression.

claim: The correlation coefficient (R) is agnostic with respect to the dependence or independence of the variables.
source_text: The data can also be described by a correlation coefficient (R) that is agnostic with respect to the dependence or independence of the variables
evidence_reasoning: This describes a property of the correlation coefficient, supported by citation to Bulmer, 1965.
